The Kresling origami of the BOT exhibits a kinematic bifurcation at a buckling threshold. Below this threshold, dynamic loads produce FA mode, whereas static loads exceeding the threshold activate a SA mode that generates sustained signals during deformation. The BOT achieves highly linear sensing of indentation depth and normal force. Its practical utility is demonstrated through a self-powered collision detection system for safety and a deep learning-based material recognition framework capable of identifying properties under electromagnetic interference (EMI) environments. This work establishes the bifurcation-gated design principle as an alternative to multi-mechanism, opening a pathway toward triboelectric tactile sensors with mechanical property perception for HRI systems.

Beyond sensing functionality, the device also exhibits efficient particulate filtration and antibacterial activity, ensuring practical wearing safety. By fusing airflow and temperature signals through a convolutional neural network model, the system achieves an overall classification accuracy of 99.17% for multiple respiratory states, including normal, slow, deep, fast breathing, and apnea. This work demonstrates a robust strategy for self-powered, humidity-resistant respiratory monitoring and highlights the potential of multimodal wearable systems for intelligent health management.

Here, we establish MERITS, a data-driven generative discovery framework integrating transport-centered electrochemical learning, mechanics-aware constraints, bounded inverse generation, and real-CIF mining to identify experimentally actionable frameworks before synthesis. It further enables > 5000 h Li symmetric cycling, 1000-cycle LiFePO4 operation, 200-cycle NCM811 operation, and soft-package-cell validation. Density functional theory and molecular dynamics link this performance to a 6.8 Å aperture near the effective TFSI− size, preferential anion regulation, accessible Li+ migration, and framework-assisted stress transfer. This work establishes a real-structure-guided design-to-device route for reducing uncertainty in multiobjective MOF/polymer electrolyte discovery. Sensitivity calculations across 11 matrix profiles further show that the workflow can be re-applied beyond PVDF-HFP after re-localizing the matrix-specific descriptor window.

items.title: Generative inverse design of microsecond-response nanostructured heat flux sensors for hypersonic aerothermal environments
items.abstract: Accurate real-time measurement of transient heat flux is vital for the operational safety of hypersonic vehicles. However, conventional heat flux sensors suffer from millisecond-to-second response delays, static-only validation schemes, and empirically driven design strategies—critical limitations that severely hinder their applicability under extreme aerothermal conditions. Herein, we propose a generative inverse design framework integrating multi-physics simulation, data-driven optimization, MEMS fabrication, and hypersonic ground validation. A coupled thermal-mechanical-electrical model is established to quantify the influences of eight geometric parameters on the sensor’s response speed, detection sensitivity, and thermomechanical stress. A deep neural network surrogate model incorporated with a conditional denoising diffusion probabilistic model is trained on 147 finite-element simulation datasets for accurate sensor performance prediction. Targeting an ultrafast response of 50 μs, we generate one million nanostructured candidate designs and further screen them comprehensively in terms of thermal stress and sensitivity via the surrogate model, ultimately identifying an optimal configuration that concurrently achieves ultrafast response, superior high-temperature stability, and high sensitivity. The optimized nanostructured heat flux sensor, fabricated via standard MEMS processes, is validated through pulsed laser tests and plasma wind tunnel experiments. It delivers a 50 μs response time—two orders of magnitude faster than state-of-the-art sensors—while maintaining exceptional stability and structural integrity under extreme plasma aerothermal conditions. The proposed generative inverse design strategy substantially shortens the development cycle of nanostructured thermal sensors and offers a practical, reliable solution for real-time, precise heat flux measurement on hypersonic vehicles in harsh environments.

items.title: Flexible piezoelectric sensor array for intelligent monitoring system of body surface morphological abnormalities
items.abstract: Real-time dynamic monitoring of body-surface morphology is crucial for the early diagnosis of progressive diseases. However, the existing passive monitoring systems are unable to perceive the dynamic changes on the body surface and is even more difficult to achieve intelligent mapping of three-dimensional morphology. Here, we propose a novel intelligent monitoring system for abnormal human body-surface morphology based on dynamic curvature detection using a 2 × 8 flexible piezoelectric sensor array. By utilizing home-made multi-channel acquisition circuit and deep learning algorithms, the system maps deformation signals of the human skin surface collected by the array into a parametric human body model, enabling personalized real-time monitoring of normal morphology and posture. An abnormal deformation recognition module in the system is to accurately identify the location and degree of local abnormal shapes on the human body surface. Moreover, a morphological perception module in the system has been developed to integrate parametric human model mapping and abnormal deformation recognition functions, achieving 3D visualization of abnormal deformations and providing clinical diagnosis support. This work overcomes the limitations of traditional passive sensors that fail to recognize morphological information, offering technical support for the continuous monitoring of body surface morphology and the intelligent recognition of home environments.

items.title: Thermoelectric cement for intelligent infrastructure
items.abstract: Cement-based thermoelectric materials offer a promising strategy to transform conventional infrastructure from passive load-bearing components into multifunctional systems capable of sensing and energy harvesting. Over the past two decades, conductive nanofillers, interface engineering, and ionically active cementitious matrices have substantially broadened the thermoelectric response accessible in these materials. Reported electrical conductivity values range from highly resistive matrices to values approaching 101 S cm–1, while reported thermopower spans from the μV K–1 to the mV K–1 range across systems with different transport regimes. However, a large thermovoltage does not necessarily translate into sustained electrical power, particularly when ionic contributions remain unresolved, and reported device-level outputs are difficult to compare across different testing and operating conditions. Beyond material-level thermoelectric optimization, practical deployment also requires transport stability, scalable manufacturing, durable interfaces, and device-level integration. This review connects transport-informed material design with scalable fabrication, device-level output, and infrastructure applications, and identifies development pathways toward deployable thermoelectric components for intelligent infrastructure.

items.title: Intelligent cellulosic fibers with ultrafast triboelectric ammonia sensing for monitoring the freshness of seafood
items.abstract: Rapid ammonia (NH3) sensing is essential for environmental monitoring, healthcare diagnostics, and food-quality assessment. However, the response kinetics of triboelectric gas sensors are often limited by inefficient conversion of gas-induced surface interactions into measurable electrical signals. Here, we report a p-type-site-mediated junction modulation strategy for constructing a cellulosic fiber-based triboelectric NH3 sensor with rapid response kinetics. The abundant oxygen-containing groups on the cellulose fibers enable the in situ growth of ZnO/p-type metal oxide (e.g., Cu, Co, Ni) heterostructures, forming an interwoven hierarchical sensing network with high surface accessibility and efficient gas-diffusion pathways. The introduced p-type metal oxide act as directional electron-trapping centers and dynamically regulate the p-n junction depletion region upon NH3 exposure. This electronic modulation amplifies the resistance variation, enhances the triboelectric output, and reverses the NH3 response polarity relative to pristine ZnO. Through the synergistic integration of heterojunction-mediated polarity regulation and the porous fibrous architecture, the sensor exhibits rapid response/recovery times (6 s and 4 s), and enables real-time monitoring of scallop freshness with strong correlation to standard freshness indicators. This work establishes an effective junction-mediated signal-transduction strategy for developing fast-response cellulosic triboelectric gas sensors.

items.title: Hierarchically programmed microarchitected origami with mechanically intelligent triboelectric outputs
items.abstract: Reconfigurable physical interfaces that transduce simple mechanical inputs into programmable electrical outputs offer promising opportunities for bioinspired sensing, multistate input devices, and human–machine interaction. The direct embedding and encoding of information within the matter’s structure through physical interaction could open up new pathways for the design of intelligent cyber-physical systems. Here, we report a hierarchically programmed microarchitected origami (HPMAO) with programmable multimodal triboelectric outputs. The HPMAO implements a synergistic macro–meso–micro three-level physical programming strategy. At the macro-scale, multi-mode folding configurations of the square-twist origami act as the first-level, supplying foundational mechanical instruction sets. At the meso-scale, a second-level program is built upon customized addressable contact architectures, where the partition of positive and negative dielectric regions forms an embedded triboelectric signal-activation array. At the micro-scale, ultrafast-laser-fabricated microstructures on dielectric (PTFE) surface serve as the third-level. These microstructures not only enlarge the library of interfacial ‘triboelectric fingerprints’ but also substantially expand the amount of accessible folding configurations of the origami substrate. The synergy of these three programming levels enables the HPMAO to map manually prescribed origami configurations to predefined multichannel electrical outputs under a single mechanical stimulus. Furthermore, by using an external machine-learning classifier, we achieve automated recognition and classification. We experimentally validate the signal-generation and information-encoding-and-decoding capabilities using a 90 mm× 90 mm prototype which can produce 64 distinct output sets, demonstrating the feasibility of encoding information with physical structure and mechanical actions. This work provides a physical signal-encoding strategy for reconfigurable multistate mechanical input interfaces in which predefined structural configurations generate distinguishable electrical outputs.
